title: Menu height can exceed available screen height making items unreachable
line: Long Global Menu menus and submenus now fit on screen and scroll, so their first items can be reached.
explanation: The Global Menu shows the app's menus as QMenus, and QMenu sizes a long menu for the whole screen height. The panel takes part of that space, so the compositor pushed the menu up past the top edge of the screen: the first items were off-screen and there was no scroll-up arrow (submenus lost their first item the same way). The applet now limits the menu and all its submenus to the screen height left free by panels, so QMenu shows scroll arrows inside the visible area.

commits.message:
applets/appmenu: keep menus within the available screen height

Long menus were sized for the whole screen, so they got pushed past the
screen edge to stay clear of the panel, hiding their first items. Limit
menus and submenus to the available screen height so they scroll.

BUG: 497515

media.caption: Before: a 70-item menu from the Global Menu starts above the screen; items 1-44 can't be reached and there is no scroll-up arrow.
After: the menu fits between the top of the screen and the panel, with a scroll arrow; hovering it scrolls back to item 1 (right).
Before: a 70-item submenu is also taller than the free space and its first item is off-screen.
After: the submenu fits on screen, starting at item 1, with a scroll-down arrow.

review.text: Capping QMenu and submenu maximumHeight in AppMenuApplet is a sensible way to make QMenu scroll within the visible area, and the before/after screenshots confirm it fixes a non-floating, always-visible bottom panel. However, Corona::availableScreenRect() excludes neither auto-hide/dodge-windows panels (leaving m_maxMenuHeight equal to the full screen height, so the bug remains unfixed there) nor the floating gap of Plasma 6's default floating panels (still overflowing by the floating margin). In addition, limitMenuHeight() only connects aboutToShow on actions already present when a menu opens, which can miss lazily populated nested submenus added asynchronously by DBusMenuImporter.
changes: Account for auto-hide, dodge-windows, and floating panels whose space is not fully subtracted from Corona::availableScreenRect(), e.g. by also bounding m_maxMenuHeight against the actual space above/below ctx->window() for TopEdge/BottomEdge panels, and verify on both floating and auto-hide panels.
Ensure nested submenus added lazily/asynchronously after aboutToShow (e.g. via QEvent::ActionAdded on watched menus) also get their maximumHeight limited.
Avoid pulling #include <QWidget> into appmenuapplet.h solely for QWIDGETSIZE_MAX (e.g. default m_maxMenuHeight to 0 and only call setMaximumHeight when positive).

reviews.text: Capping the QMenu and its submenus to Corona::availableScreenRect is the right place for this: on Wayland QMenu can't know about panels, so the applet that positions the popup has to tell it, and it falls back to QScreen::availableGeometry cleanly. The before/after shots show the 70-item menu and submenu now fit between the screen edge and the panel with scroll arrows and item 1 reachable, and the top-panel and short-menu cases were checked. Nitpicks: the menu still opens scrolled to its last items while the pointer rests on the button (QMenu behaviour, items are reachable now), and submenus added to a DBusMenu after their parent's aboutToShow only get the cap on their next opening.
